summary30s: The Indian Constitution was drafted by the Constituent Assembly between December 1946 and November 1949, comprising 300 members after Partition (82% Congress members).

Six individuals played pivotal roles: Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajendra Prasad (President of Assembly), B.R. Ambedkar (Drafting Committee Chairman), K.M. Munshi, and Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer.
Nehru moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' on 13 December 1946, outlining the ideals of an Independent Sovereign Republic committed to justice, equality, and freedom.
Demands for separate electorates were rejected as divisive by Sardar Patel and Govind Ballabh Pant, while safeguards for Depressed Classes and Adivasis (led by Jaipal Singh) were enshrined.

The language dispute between Hindi enthusiasts (R.V. Dhulekar) and non-Hindi speakers was resolved through the Language Committee's compromise: Hindi in Devanagari script became the 'Official Language', not 'National Language'.

coreConcepts.title: The Constituent Assembly: Composition and Key Roles
coreConcepts.explanation: The Constituent Assembly had 300 members (originally 389 before Partition). While the Congress held 82% of seats, it accommodated diverse viewpoints: socialists, capitalists, conservatives, and social reformers. Six key individuals shaped proceedings: three from Congress (Jawaharlal Nehru who moved the Objectives Resolution; Vallabhbhai Patel who worked behind the scenes drafting compromise reports; and Dr. Rajendra Prasad who presided as President of the Assembly); two eminent constitutional lawyers (Dr. B.R. Ambedkar who served as Chairman of the Drafting Committee; and K.M. Munshi from Gujarat); and Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer from Madras. They were assisted by two civil servants: Constitutional Advisor B.N. Rau (prepared background papers on global constitutions) and Chief Draughtsman S.N. Mukherjee (translated complex legal ideas into precise legislative drafting).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Themes in Indian History Part III, Section 1
coreConcepts.examTip: B.N. Rau = Constitutional Advisor; S.N. Mukherjee = Chief Draughtsman; B.R. Ambedkar = Chairman of Drafting Committee.

coreConcepts.title: The Objectives Resolution (13 December 1946)
coreConcepts.explanation: On 13 December 1946, Jawaharlal Nehru introduced the historic 'Objectives Resolution'. It outlined the defining ideals of the Constitution: proclaiming India as an 'Independent Sovereign Republic', guaranteeing citizens justice, equality, and freedom, and providing adequate safeguards for minorities, backward and tribal areas, and depressed classes. Nehru emphasized that India was not simply copying Western constitutions (American or French), but adapting universal ideals to the unique genius of the Indian people. Communist member Somnath Lahiri pointed out that the Assembly was functioning under the shadow of British imperialism; Nehru agreed but emphasized that the Assembly derived its authority from the passion of the Indian masses.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Themes in Indian History Part III, Section 2: 'The Vision of the Constitution'
coreConcepts.examTip: Objectives Resolution: Moved by Nehru on 13 Dec 1946; laid the foundation for the Preamble of the Constitution.

coreConcepts.title: Debates on Rights: Separate Electorates vs Reserved Seats
coreConcepts.explanation: On 27 August 1947, B. Pocker Bahadur from Madras made a powerful plea for continuing separate electorates for Muslims. This sparked fierce opposition. Sardar Patel condemned separate electorates as a 'poison that has entered the body politic of our country' which caused Partition. Govind Ballabh Pant declared separate electorates suicidal for minorities because it isolated them permanently. Begum Aizaz Rasul (a Muslim member) also agreed that separate electorates were self-destructive. Regarding the Depressed Castes, Dr. Ambedkar abandoned his earlier demand for separate electorates after the 1932 Poona Pact, advocating reservation of seats in legislatures alongside the abolition of untouchability (Article 17). Jaipal Singh, representing Adivasis, spoke eloquently of 6,000 years of dispossession, demanding reserved legislative representation and constitutional protection for tribals.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Themes in Indian History Part III, Section 3: 'Defining Rights'
coreConcepts.examTip: Jaipal Singh = Representative of Adivasis in the Constituent Assembly; Begum Aizaz Rasul = Opposed separate electorates for Muslims.

coreConcepts.title: Federalism and the National Language Compromise
coreConcepts.explanation: The Assembly debated the balance of power between the Centre and the States. Drafted after the trauma of Partition, the Constitution created a strong Union. Three lists were crafted: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List; Article 356 gave the Centre power to take over provincial administration. K. Santhanam from Madras warned that overburdening the Centre with fiscal and administrative functions would weaken it, advocating greater financial resources for states. The language debate was the most contentious: R.V. Dhulekar made an aggressive pitch for Hindi as the national language. This provoked deep anxiety among members from South India (Shrimati G. Durgabai, T.A. Ramalingam Chettiar). The Language Committee arrived at a compromise formula: Hindi in the Devanagari script would be the 'Official Language' of the Union (NOT the National Language); English would continue to be used for all official purposes for a transition period of 15 years; and provinces could choose regional languages for provincial administration.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Themes in Indian History Part III, Sections 4 & 5
coreConcepts.examTip: Crucial distinction: Hindi is the OFFICIAL language (Rajbhasha) of the Union, NOT the National language (Rashtrabhasha).

workedExamples.question:
On which date did Jawaharlal Nehru move the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly?
(A) 9 December 1946
(B) 11 December 1946
(C) 13 December 1946
(D) 26 November 1949
workedExamples.explanation: On 13 December 1946, Jawaharlal Nehru introduced the 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly, defining the ideals that were to guide the framing of the Constitution.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: 9 Dec 1946 = First sitting of the Constituent Assembly.
Step 2: 11 Dec 1946 = Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected permanent President.
Step 3: 13 Dec 1946 = Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution.
Step 4: 26 Nov 1949 = Constitution adopted and enacted.
solutionSteps: Step 1: 9 Dec 1946 = First sitting of the Constituent Assembly.
Step 2: 11 Dec 1946 = Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected permanent President.
Step 3: 13 Dec 1946 = Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution.
Step 4: 26 Nov 1949 = Constitution adopted and enacted.

workedExamples.question:
Who served as the Constitutional Advisor to the Government of India during the drafting of the Constitution, preparing comprehensive comparative background papers?
(A) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
(B) Sir B.N. Rau
(C) S.N. Mukherjee
(D) Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer
workedExamples.explanation: Sir B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor to the Government of India. He prepared a series of background papers based on a close study of the political systems of other countries.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Ambedkar was Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
Step 2: B.N. Rau was Constitutional Advisor.
Step 3: S.N. Mukherjee was Chief Draughtsman.
Conclusion: Option B (Sir B.N. Rau) is correct.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Differentiating between advisory, drafting, and presiding roles in the Assembly.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: Who famously declared in the Constituent Assembly that separate electorates were 'a poison that has entered the body politic of our country'?

According to the Constituent Assembly's Language Committee compromise, Hindi in Devanagari script was declared as the: (A) National Language, (B) Official Language, (C) Lingua Franca, (D) State Language.
howCuetAsks.strategy: Official Language of the Union (Rajbhasha), NOT National Language.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing Hindi was made the 'National Language' of India by the Constitution.
commonTraps.correctConcept: The Constitution does NOT declare Hindi as the 'National Language'. The Language Committee designated Hindi in Devanagari script as the 'OFFICIAL Language' (Rajbhasha) of the Union.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Common popular belief conflates Official Language with National Language.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: Hindi is the Official Language, NOT the National Language.

commonTraps.misconception: Confusing B.N. Rau with S.N. Mukherjee.
commonTraps.correctConcept: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor; S.N. Mukherjee was the Chief Draughtsman.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Both were civil servants working closely with Ambedkar, leading to name confusion.

practiceQuestions.question: Who among the following was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the Chief Draughtsman of the Constituent Assembly who had the ability to put complex proposals into clear legal language?
practiceQuestions.explanation: S.N. Mukherjee was the Chief Draughtsman, whose ability to translate intricate proposals into clear legal language was praised by Ambedkar.

practiceQuestions.question: Who represented the Adivasis in the Constituent Assembly and spoke passionately about their historical dispossession and the need for protection?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Jaipal Singh, a gifted speaker and hockey Olympian representing the Adivasis, made a moving speech on tribal rights.

practiceQuestions.question: Which Muslim woman member of the Constituent Assembly spoke against separate electorates, arguing they were self-destructive for minorities?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Begum Aizaz Rasul felt that separate electorates were self-destructive since they isolated the minorities from the majority.

practiceQuestions.question: Which member from Madras warned the Assembly that overburdening the Centre with responsibilities and starving the provinces of funds would cripple both?
practiceQuestions.explanation: K. Santhanam from Madras defended states' rights and warned that an over-centralized state would break down under its own weight.

practiceQuestions.question: Under the Language Committee compromise, how was Hindi in the Devanagari script designated in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: The Official Language (Rajbhasha) of the Union
The exclusive language for courts and parliament
The language of education throughout India

practiceQuestions.explanation: The Language Committee decided that Hindi in the Devanagari script would be the official language of the Union, not the national language.

practiceQuestions.question: For how many years was English permitted to continue being used for all official purposes of the Union following the commencement of the Constitution?
practiceQuestions.explanation: For the first fifteen years, English would continue to be used for all official purposes.

practiceQuestions.question: Which member of the Constituent Assembly aggressively asserted: 'People who are present in this House to fashion a constitution for India and do not know Hindustani are not worthy to be members of this Assembly'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: R.V. Dhulekar, a Congressman from the United Provinces, made this uncompromising statement on 10 December 1946.

practiceQuestions.question: How many members actually signed the Constitution of India when it was finally adopted on 26 November 1949?
practiceQuestions.explanation: On 26 November 1949, 284 members were actually present and affixed their signatures to the historic document.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The Constituent Assembly drafted a Constitution that created an exceptionally strong Central Government.
Reason (R): The violence of Partition, fears of balkanisation, and chaotic refugee crises convinced leaders that only a powerful Centre could maintain peace, coordinate economic planning, and defend national sovereignty.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: The historical context of Partition trauma and fears of chaos compelled the Assembly to prioritize a powerful Union over loose provincial decentralization. Both are true and (R) explains (A).
